chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, so he locked the door, and pulled the curtain, and touched, and kissed. Then he divorced her. Is the dower obligated upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: The dower is not obligated upon him except by copulation.

key_terms.الصَّدَاقَ: The dower or dowry given to the wife

ai.seo_question: What action is required to obligate the full dower in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential threshold for the full dower (mahr al-mithl) by distinguishing between preliminary intimacy and consummation. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while the husband is entitled to the wife's companionship upon contracting the marriage, the complete financial obligation is only triggered by actual sexual intercourse (wiqaa'), a principle that underpins the Shia legal distinction between partial and full dower in cases of divorce prior to consummation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who married a woman, so he locked the door, and pulled the curtain, and touched, and kissed. Then he divorced her. Is the dower Obligated upon him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The dower is not Obligated upon him except by the copulation’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who marries a woman, closes the door, pulls the curtains, touches and kisses her; then divorces; if mahr (dower) becomes obligatory. He (the Imam) said, ‘Mahr (dower) becomes obligatory only after sexual intercourse.’”
